questions: Who am I?
I had been away for a long time.
I worried about meeting someone in my family.
I sent presents ahead to my brother Esav.
Who am I?
Someone was nervous about seeing me.
I arrived with a large group of men.
I ran to hug my brother Yaakov.
What are we?
We reached someone before our owner did.
We were meant to help make peace.
Yaakov sent us to Esav: goats, sheep and other animals.
What am I?
You can do me even when you feel afraid.
Yaakov did me before meeting his brother.
He asked Hashem to save him.
Who am I?
My family was already very big when I arrived.
My mother had one older son, Yosef.
I am Rachel's younger son, born in this parsha.
What number am I?
Hearing me made Yaakov worried.
I counted people, not presents.
I am the number of men coming with Esav.
What am I?
I was part of a plan for danger.
If one group was attacked, another could escape.
Yaakov divided his people and animals into this many camps.
Who am I?
I met Yaakov when he was alone.
Our struggle lasted until dawn.
I injured his thigh, then gave him a bracha before leaving.
What am I?
I was given after a difficult struggle.
I am still used for Yaakov's descendants.
I am Yaakov's other name.
Who am I?
My family kept traveling after I died.
A monument marked my grave beside the road.
I am Binyamin's mother, buried near Beis Lechem.
What am I?
I affect what goes on a Jewish plate.
My story begins with an injury during a struggle.
We do not eat this sinew, remembering Yaakov's injured thigh.
Whose pace?
Esav offered to travel together.
Yaakov feared pushing his flocks too hard.
He would go slowly to suit which members of his group?
Where am I?
Yaakov had been here before.
Hashem told him to return and build a mizbeach.
My name means "House of Hashem."
Who are we?
We are brothers who acted together.
Yaakov objected to what we did in a city.
We attacked Shechem after our sister Dinah was harmed.
Where am I?
Several family members rest here.
Avraham bought me many years earlier.
Esav and Yaakov buried Yitzchak in me.
silly_round: Yaakov sent Esav a gift of four hundred rubber ducks.
Yaakov said: Hurry! The little children can run all day!
He planned to travel at their pace.
